# sync-engine

> sync-engine is an ESM-only TypeScript library for composing independently implemented stateful behaviors. Concepts own state and behavior; reactions, views, formers, and endpoints connect them at the application level.

This index is for human and software agents that use sync-engine to design,
build, call, or operate an application. It does not describe changes to the
sync-engine repository.

The current release is beta, and only the newest beta is supported. Pin an exact package version and read the [support policy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mit-sdg/sync-engine/main/SUPPORT.md) before upgrading or deploying it.

## HTTP transport

- [HTTP Public API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mit-sdg/sync-engine/main/packages/http/public-surface.md) — supported HTTP subpaths, exports, signatures, and defaults
- Install the exact same beta of `@mit-sdg/sync-engine-http` and `@mit-sdg/sync-engine`; the HTTP package declares an exact core peer dependency.
- Import handlers and policies from `@mit-sdg/sync-engine-http/server`, fetch clients from `@mit-sdg/sync-engine-http/client`, and `httpWire` from `@mit-sdg/sync-engine-http/tooling`. The companion root and deep imports are unsupported.
- Put public domain-error mappings on the reused HTTP profile or floor. Generate the public contract with `projections: [httpWire({ policy, name })]`.
- Core contains no HTTP handler or fetch-client exports. Use `bindTransport` and `createClient` for a custom transport without the companion package.

## Working rules

- Use only the package subpaths listed in the Public API. The package root and deep imports are unsupported.
- Keep concept implementations independent of peer concepts and application composition.
- Treat generated TypeScript as a caller contract. Add explicit validators for
  runtime values.
- Do not assume transactions across actions, rollback, replay, restart recovery, distributed serialization, cancellation of accepted work, or exactly-once execution.
- Change application source declarations, regenerate artifacts, and review the
  generated diff.
- Use the reference pages for guarantees. Guides, examples, and generated read-back demonstrate particular constructions.
